instruction.text: What is physical contact? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: The topic of physical contact goes hand-in-hand with ((++personal_boundaries food)). Physical contact is touching or being touched by someone.
It’s up to ((++you your_friends)) to decide what forms of physical contact you are comfortable with.

instruction.text: What are some examples of physical contact? Select all the correct answers.
What are some forms of physical contact that are never okay and are considered inappropriate? Select the three correct answers.

hint.text: Inappropriate means behaviour that is wrong and should not be allowed in certain cases. For example, an adult trying to harm or touch a child.
hint.label: Inappropriate

feedback.end: If you or someone you know ever encounter any of these, you must always report it to a trusted adult. This could be your parent or guardian, or a teacher at school.

b: a teacher holding your hand when you cross the street
your friend giving you a hug

instruction.text: Decide if the physical contact being described is okay or not okay.

hint.text: Remember that you should always have someone’s permission before any physical contact with them. As long as it’s not inappropriate, and you never force it, it is usually okay!

atoms.a: tickling someone when they’re telling you to stop
kissing a classmate you like on the cheek as a surprise
hitting someone when they’ve made you upset
you and your friend going in for a hug together
reaching out to hold someone’s hand

feedback.end: Although most people might be okay with gentle physical contact, such as high-fives, hugs and holding hands, there may be certain cases in which they are not. Keep in mind that there are also people who do not want to be touched at all. The key is to always check with people first!

instruction.text: How should you respond to unwanted physical contact that makes you uncomfortable? Select the three correct answers.

trainers.feedback: You should always be as firm as possible if someone is trying to touch you in a way that hurts you or makes you uncomfortable.

b: ++say that it hurts or makes you uncomfortable

instruction.text: What should you do if this unwanted physical contact continues even after you tell them to stop? Select the three correct answers.

feedback.end:
It might be scary, but you must always report someone who is repeatedly trying to inappropriately touch or hurt you. Make sure that the person you are talking to will take action.

If you can’t talk to anyone around you, you should contact Childline on 0800 1111 or, in an emergency, the police on 999.

b: bully someone to let out your anger
